cycles.summary: Corrected five errors that could cause harm: 112 described as a unified dispatcher, a flat 10-minute shelter exit rule, SAHAR marked as closed, five Level-1 trauma centers, and the superseded two-finger infant CPR technique. Added non-voice emergency channels, poison control and sexual assault lines to the numbers table, and the referral and night ER copay tiers.

lessons: CARRY RESOLVED: terrorist infiltration, hazardous materials, tsunami, prolonged stay and siren-system disruption are now covered verbatim in references/oref-scenarios.md from the Home Front Command guidelines.

CARRY RESOLVED: MDA statistics re-sourced to MDA's own 2024 annual summary (206 stations, 2,650+ vehicles, ~37,500 personnel). The 8-minute average response time was REMOVED, not caveated: MDA publishes no such figure and it was being repeated as reassurance inside a worked example about someone collapsing.

CARRY RESOLVED: 101, 105, 110 and 118 are now cited at their operating authority's own site, and the deaf/hard-of-hearing channels now carry actual contact details (police SMS 052-2020100 / fax 08-6525111 / Listen@police.gov.il, welfare silent-call SMS 050-2270118, 105 WhatsApp 052-1210105). The previous version said the channels existed but gave a deaf user no way to use them.

SAFETY-CRITICAL CORRECTION: the 'at least 10 minutes for rocket fire' rule does not exist in current Home Front Command guidance. Rockets and ballistic missiles are ONE merged guideline whose exit rule is open-ended ('עד לקבלת הנחיה מפורשת מפיקוד העורף'). The two-regime framing the previous cycle introduced was itself the defect. The only guideline containing 10 minutes is siren-system disruption, a different scenario, and that is where every 'wait 10 minutes' answer in circulation comes from. Finding this required a POSITIVE search for where the number DOES live, not just a negative check that it was absent from the rocket page.

The ER figures 1,199 / 269 / 259 were all wrong. The referral case is a FULL exemption, not a 269 NIS reduced fee, so the skill was telling entitled users to pay. The night window is 01:00-06:00 and waives the treatment cost only; there is no 23:00 boundary anywhere in the regulations. Current tariff is 1,241 (code 5044) and 281 (code 00964), effective 1.7.2026.

The evidence gate is near-blind to this skill. It extracted 6-7 facts from a document made almost entirely of phone numbers, timings and protocol steps, and it went green in that state on the previous cycle while the shelter rule was wrong. A green gate here is evidence of nothing. Every safety claim in this cycle was verified by hand against the operating authority.

Eight LEGACY evidence entries had fabricated or mismatched snippets, including one asserting blood donation is open from age 17 and one asserting asthma triggers a full ER exemption, both contradicted by the skill's own text. A skill can pass the self-consistency gate for cycles with an evidence file that actively disagrees with it. Run --check-sources, not just the default pass.

The Expert returned TWELVE criticals, all in the areas references/domain-checklist.md had already recorded as 'not re-verified against a guideline source'. The checklist predicted exactly where the defects were and the previous version shipped anyway. Treat that marker as BLOCKING, not as a note.

first-aid-basics.md contained a direct internal contradiction: two rows told a lone rescuer to do 2 minutes of CPR before calling 101, and a bolded line two rows below said 'Calling is the first action, not the last'. It also printed a 30:2 paediatric algorithm with no initial rescue breaths while declaring in the same file that Israeli courses follow ERC, which opens with 5. Both are fixed. Anaphylaxis, stroke, hypoglycaemia, seizures, carbon monoxide, drowning, scorpion sting and the recovery position were absent entirely and are now added.

The skill refused on principle to quote an MDA response time and then quoted unsourced ER triage and Terem wait times. Both are removed, and the missing instruction (go back to the triage nurse if you deteriorate) is added.

A LEGAL NOTICE was added this cycle. Adding clinical protocol content (adrenaline dosing, CPR ratios) tripped verify_legal.py, which the skill had previously passed. The gate was right: the skill now emits clinical instruction and needed a medical notice, not a bureaucratic one.

deferred.text: Every hospital phone number in references/hospital-directory.md has STILL never been verified against each hospital's own site, now across three cycles. A spot check this cycle found Rambam publishes a switchboard AND separate ER numbers which the directory does not distinguish. This is the largest remaining hazard in the skill. Next cycle must treat it as blocking.

Radiological event, cluster rocket fire, blast, the two earthquake guidelines, means-of-alert, and Home Front Command's disability guidance are named in references/oref-scenarios.md but not quoted from the source.

100, 102, 104, 110-as-dispatcher, 112, and the candidates 119 / 1-800-220-000 / 103 still have no citation at the operating authority's own site. gov.il 403s curl for every path and needs a browser session per page.
The mass-casualty and uninsured-person sections of references/triage-and-red-flags.md are written from practice and are not quoted from a cited source.

Expert MAJOR M5 (ambulance charges) was added in summary only; the actual MDA transport tariff and the refund routes are not sourced. M11 (cardiac chest-pain bystander protocol) is not yet in the first-aid file.
The skill says the tariff is revised several times a year; an older evidence note says 1 January annually. Reconcile against the MoH price-list collector.

lessons.text: Emergency numbers in this catalog were originally sourced to aggregators. In this skill, 100 and 102 were cited to a personal Israel-info page, 104 and the shelter rule to an olim NGO, and the trauma-center claim to an olim services site that encoded the error. A sibling skill in the same batch was found to have four of six crisis lines wrong. Every number must be read off its own operator's page, in a text layer, before it ships.

The OREF URL backing all three shelter-timing claims returns HTTP 200 with a 9-byte body. A status-code-only link checker passes it. Link validation for this skill must assert on body length and content, not on the response code.

oref.org.il, gov.il, mdais.org and natal.org.il all refuse automated fetch by curl, WebFetch and text-render proxies. A 403 or an anomalous status from these hosts means the source needs a browser session, never that the source should be removed.

Every claim in this skill's evidence file listed appears_in as SKILL.md and SKILL_HE.md only. The reference files and metadata.json sat outside the net, which is how the five-trauma-centers error survived in three files at once. appears_in must enumerate every file the claim actually appears in.

The Gotchas section half-corrected the 112 claim while the body and the troubleshooting section still asserted the opposite. An agent reading top-down acts on the body, so a correction that lives only in Gotchas is not a correction.

During this cycle the Playwright browser was shared across ten agents and returned documents from other agents' navigations twice. Browser reads must be treated as untrusted unless the returned page URL matches the requested URL. All findings in this cycle were taken from curl, pdftotext and direct fetch instead.

deferred.text: Four of seven official Home Front Command scenario categories are absent: terrorist infiltration, hazardous materials, radiological event, and tsunami. Deliberately deferred from the 1.4.0 cycle to keep the change surface small. Tracked in references/domain-checklist.md. Terrorist infiltration is the highest-priority of the four.

Siren and shelter guidance sits at Step 8 of 9, behind ER copays and blood donation, and the mental-health crisis lines at Step 7. For a skill whose highest-stakes query is a siren in progress, the order should be numbers, then siren and shelter, then red-flag symptoms, then everything else. Deferred from 1.4.0.

The skill routes users to a kupat cholim clinic for non-urgent care but lists no way to reach one out of hours. The Ministry of Health page already linked by the skill lists 24/7 mental-health lines for all four HMOs, and states that psychiatric emergency rooms are open 24/7 with no referral and no charge. Verify each shortcode at its own HMO before publishing.

Numbers still not confirmed at their own operator's site: 101, 102, 104, 105, 118 and NATAL *3362. Also unadded for lack of verification: 119 National Cyber Directorate, the 1-800-220-000 domestic violence hotline, and 103 Israel Electric. These need one uncontended browser session.

Before this cycle the evidence file contained zero citations for any first-aid step across a 297-line reference file. Infant CPR and adult choking are now cited. Bleeding, tourniquets, burns, heatstroke, snake bite and jellyfish are still uncited, and drowning and opioid overdose are absent.

Station count, ambulance count, the 800-donations-per-day figure and the average 8-minute response time are uncited or cited to a newspaper culture article. The response-time figure is repeated as reassurance inside a worked example about someone collapsing in the street, which reads as a promise. Either source it to MDA's published annual figures or cut it.

Every hospital phone number in references/hospital-directory.md was carried over from earlier versions and has never been verified. A caveat was added in this cycle; verification is still outstanding.
